slides.title: Pricing in 2027 while churn is rising
Key questions

claims.claim: Should Palisade raise prices in 2027 while churn is rising and, if so, where and by how much, to grow ARR at least 15% with net revenue retention above 100%?
evidence: Decision maker: CEO, deciding the 2027 pricing plan with the leadership team
Success criteria: ARR up at least 15% in 2027, from $86.0M; Net revenue retention above 100% overall; Price changes only at renewal, and within enterprise contract terms
Timing: Leadership meeting on the 2027 pricing plan, December 2026
Out of scope: New plans or packaging to answer Inkwell; Renegotiating enterprise price caps; The 2027 new-customer sales plan

Sub-questions: 1 Is rising churn a sign that customers reject our price? 2 Will mid-market and enterprise customers accept a rise at renewal? 3 Can SMB take a rise now that Inkwell sells at $9? 4 What does each option add to ARR, and does it reach 15%? 5 How should we roll out the rise in 2027?

slides.title: Executive summary

claims.claim: Raise prices in 2027 where customers stay for the product, and test SMB before touching it
Rising churn comes from the 2025 promotion, not from core customers leaving over price
evidence: Other SMB churn is 2.1% a month, from 2.0% a year earlier
Better onboarding of the cohort cuts SMB churn by a tenth, not half

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise are the safer place for a 10% rise at renewal
evidence: A 10% higher price did not slow 2024 mid-market sign-ups
Enterprise adds only about $0.8M, as 40% of its ARR renews in 2027

claims.claim: An SMB rise is a bet on Inkwell: it breaks even at twice the 2023 reaction
evidence: Our win rate against Inkwell fell from 51% to 38%
An 8% rise on non-promotion SMB nets about $0.7M

claims.claim: The targeted rise adds about $4.3M and keeps the 15% target in reach
evidence: The 12% plan yields about $7.6M, not $10.3M
New customers need to add only about $0.6M of ARR

claims.claim: Reprice where customers stay in January, and test SMB in Q1
evidence: The promotion cohort keeps today's price and gets an activation push

slides.title: Churn is a promotion problem
Churn is rising because of the 2025 promotion, not because core customers reject our price

claims.claim: The rise sits in SMB; mid-market moved a little and enterprise not at all
evidence: 1.1 pp rise in SMB monthly logo churn, H1 2025 to H1 2026

claims.claim: Inside SMB, the 2025 promotion cohort accounts for the rise
evidence: 2.1% monthly churn of SMB customers outside the promotion, against 2.0% a year earlier

claims.claim: Price complaints rose only among promotion customers who lost their discount
evidence: 18% of non-promotion SMB churners cite price, against 19% of all SMB churners in 2025

claims.claim: Onboarding helps, but it cannot halve SMB churn as Customer Success expects
evidence: 41% of promotion customers sent five documents in month one, against 72% of others

slides.title: 1a: The churn rise sits in SMB, a segment with 80% of our customers but only 24% of ARR

claims.claim: SMB: Churn up 1.1 pp; the only real rise
evidence: SMB: 80% of customers, 24% of ARR, churn H1 2025 2%, H1 2026 3.1%, NRR 94%

claims.claim: Mid-market: Up 0.2 pp from a low base; cause not yet known
evidence: Mid-market: 18% of customers, 48% of ARR, churn 0.6% → 0.8%, NRR 112%

claims.claim: Enterprise: Flat churn and the highest retention
evidence: Enterprise: 2% of customers, 28% of ARR, churn 0.2% → 0.2%, NRR 118%

claims.claim: Board figure "1.4% → 2.3%": see backup

slides.title: 1b: Inside SMB, the rise comes from the promotion cohort, while churn among other SMB customers barely moved

claims.claim: A third of SMB customers, over half of those who leave
evidence: Monthly churn: Other SMB H1 2025 2.0%; Other SMB H1 2026 2.1%; Promotion cohort H1 2026 4.9%
All SMB, H1 2026 3.1%
the cohort is 36% of SMB customers but about 56% of those lost each month

claims.claim: Promotion cohort: 2,100 customers who joined at 50% off in February–August 2025; most who left did so within two months of the discount ending
Other SMB: up only 0.1 percentage point in a year, even after Inkwell's $9 plan arrived in October 2025
estimated monthly churn of the cohort 4.9%; the brief does not report it
evidence: 103 promotion customers lost a month (183 − 80) ÷ 2,100 promotion customers still in the base = 4.9%
Cohort churn compared with other SMB 2.3x (4.9% ÷ 2.1%)
183 = 5,900 SMB customers × 3.1%; 80 = 3,800 other SMB customers × 2.1%. H1 2026 average rates applied to mid-2026 customer counts

slides.title: 1c: The jump in price as an exit reason comes from promotion customers, not from the core SMB base

claims.claim: Losing the discount, not our list price, drives these exits
evidence: Share citing price: Promotion churners H1 2026 52%; All SMB churners H1 2026 34%; All SMB churners H1 2025 19%; Other SMB churners H1 2026 18%

claims.claim: Promotion churners: most left within two months of the 50% discount ending, so "price" means paying full price for the first time
All SMB: the rise is a mix effect, because promotion customers are now about 56% of those who leave (1b)
Other SMB churners: the share naming price is flat, even with Inkwell's cheaper plan on the market
evidence: Exit survey: share of churned customers who answered; response rates are not given in the briefing pack

slides.title: 1d: Weak activation explains only about 30% of the promotion cohort's extra churn

claims.claim: Weak activation explains only about 30% of the promotion cohort's extra churn
evidence: 0.8 pp extra churn weak activation predicts: 2.9% at 41% active, with inactive customers churning 3 times as often, less 2.1%
2.8 pp extra churn the cohort shows: about 4.9% (1b) less 2.1% for other SMB customers
0.8 pp ÷ 2.8 pp = 30% share of the cohort's extra churn that onboarding could reach

claims.claim: The estimate is generous to onboarding
evidence: Customers sending fewer than five documents in month one churn about three times as often as the rest, in both cohorts
Other SMB customers' 2.1% churn, with 72% active, sets the churn of each activation group
Activating promotion customers now works as well as in their first month, which flatters the programme

claims.claim: The remaining 2 percentage points most likely reflect the end of the discount
evidence: 52% of promotion churners name price (1c)

slides.title: 1d: Lifting the promotion cohort to other customers' activation would cut SMB churn by about a tenth, not the half hoped for

claims.claim: Onboarding is worth doing, but it is not the fix
evidence: SMB monthly churn: SMB today 3.1%; Cohort as active as others 2.8%; Cohort at other-SMB churn 2.1%; Customer Success goal 1.55%
165 SMB customers lost a month (80 + 85) ÷ 5,900 SMB customers = 2.8%
80 = 3,800 other SMB customers × 2.1%; 85 = 2,100 promotion customers × 4.1%, their churn at 72% active (1d)
Customer Success: "An onboarding programme will halve SMB churn within two quarters"

claims.claim: Every customer active: even then SMB churn would fall only about 18%, to 2.5% a month
Halving: would need the cohort to churn about 0.5% a month, a quarter of the rate of other SMB customers

slides.title: 2c: Contract terms hold the 2027 enterprise price gain to about $0.8M, because most enterprise ARR does not renew

evidence: Enterprise ARR ($M): Not renewing in 2027 14.4; Renews, capped at 7% 5.76; Renews, no cap 3.84

claims.claim: No cap: these renewals can take the same 10% as mid-market; retention of 118% says they value the product
2027 ARR gain from enterprise pricing $0.8M
evidence: $9.6M enterprise ARR renewing in 2027: 40% of $24.0M
× 60% share of enterprise ARR under 7% caps, assumed the same among renewals = $5.8M renewing ARR that can rise by 7% at most

claims.claim: No price test covered enterprise; the case rests on 118% retention, 0.2% monthly churn and the advisory board finding

slides.title: Churn is a promotion problem
An SMB price rise is a bet that Inkwell has not changed how our customers react to price

claims.claim: Inkwell undercuts our SMB plan and has already cut our win rate
evidence: 38% win rate in SMB deals where Inkwell was considered, H1 2026, against 51% a year earlier

claims.claim: The 2023 rise lifted churn for six months and left it a little higher
evidence: 1.9% SMB monthly churn once it settled after the 2023 rise, against 1.8% before

claims.claim: An 8% rise pays only if customers react less than about twice as strongly as in 2023

evidence: List price $ per user per month: Palisade SMB after 12% 16.8; Palisade SMB today 15; Inkwell Starter 9

claims.claim: Our win rate where Inkwell is considered fell by 13 percentage points in a year
evidence: −13 pp

claims.claim: A 12% rise would put our SMB plan at 1.9 times Inkwell's price, on the deals we are already losing
evidence: Inkwell launched Starter in October 2025; Inkwell Pro sells at $24 against $29 for Palisade Business

slides.title: 3b: The 2023 SMB rise lifted churn for six months and left it a notch higher, and that was before Inkwell

claims.claim: Churn recovered, but not fully
evidence: SMB monthly churn around the 2023 8% rise: Before the rise 1.8%; First six months 2.3%; After it settled 1.9%
First six months: churn ran half a percentage point a month above its old level
After: it settled 0.1 percentage point higher and stayed there

claims.claim: 3.6% extra share of SMB customers lost in the first year after the 8% rise
evidence: 0.5 pp extra churn a month for six months + 0.1 pp for the next six months = 3.6% (0.5 × 6 + 0.1 × 6)

claims.claim: Then and now: no rival sold a $9 plan in 2023, so this is a floor for 2027, not a forecast

slides.title: 3c: An 8% rise on non-promotion SMB nets about $0.7M at the 2023 reaction and breaks even at about twice that

claims.claim: An 8% rise on non-promotion SMB nets about $0.7M at the 2023 reaction and breaks even at about twice that
evidence: $1.3M price gain: 8% on $16.6M of non-promotion SMB ARR, all of which renews in 2027
− $0.6M ARR lost if customers react as in 2023: 3.6% more customers leave (3b), at the higher price
= $0.7M net gain in 2027; it reaches zero if the reaction is 2.1 times as strong

claims.claim: The case holds the promotion cohort out and scales 2023's reaction
evidence: The 2,100 promotion customers ($4.4M of ARR) keep today's price
Each extra lost customer counts at a full year of ARR, which overstates the loss
Effects of a higher list price on new-customer win rates are left out

claims.claim: How Inkwell changed existing customers' reaction is unknown; a Q1 test can settle it (5a)

slides.title: Churn is a promotion problem
A targeted rise keeps the 15% growth target in reach without the SMB bet of the 12% plan

claims.claim: The 12% plan yields about $7.6M of ARR in 2027, not the $10.3M quoted
evidence: $10.3M of ARR claimed for 12% on every plan; renewals and caps cut it before any churn

evidence: 15% ARR growth objective for 2027, from $86.0M

slides.title: 4a: The 12% plan would add about $7.6M of ARR in 2027, not $10.3M, before a single customer reacts

claims.claim: The $10.3M assumes every dollar of ARR reprices in 2027

claims.claim: Enterprise not renewing: the largest cut, because 60% of enterprise ARR sits in contracts that run past 2027
Mid-market not renewing: 15% of mid-market ARR renews only in 2028
Caps: renewing enterprise contracts under a 7% cap cannot take the full 12%
evidence: $5.8M enterprise ARR renewing in 2027 under a 7% cap (2c) × −5 pp part of the 12% the cap blocks = −$0.3M ARR gain lost to caps

claims.claim: Before churn: SMB reaction would cut it further (backup)

slides.title: 4b: Mid-market carries the targeted rise: $3.5M of its $4.3M comes from 10% at mid-market renewals

claims.claim: A third of the growth target, from the segments that stay for the product
evidence: ARR gain ($M): Mid-market, 10% 3.485; Enterprise, 10% or 7% cap 0.787
$3.5M mid-market: 85% of $41.0M renews × 10% + $0.8M enterprise: $5.8M capped × 7% + $3.8M uncapped × 10% (2c) = $4.3M added to ARR by the end of 2027, before any churn reaction
Share of the $12.9M growth target 33% ($4.3M ÷ $12.9M)

claims.claim: Mid-market: 85% of its $41.0M renews in 2027, and all of it can take the tested 10%
Enterprise: small in 2027, because the rest reprices only as multi-year contracts come up
SMB: held at $15 in the base plan; a passed Q1 test adds up to $1.3M before churn, about $0.7M net (3c)
12% instead of 10% in mid-market: about $0.7M more, beyond the level tested

slides.title: 4b: At today's retention, new customers need to add only about $0.6M of ARR to reach the 2027 target

claims.claim: Retention: each percentage point of overall retention is worth about $0.86M of ARR
If retention slips a point: new customers would need to bring about $1.5M
New customers: the 2027 sales plan is not in this briefing; the 2025 promotion alone brought $4.4M of ARR
Confirm a 2027 new-business plan of at least $1.5M of ARR, so the target survives a weaker year

slides.title: 4c: Overall net revenue retention has ample headroom: SMB would have to fall to 56% to break the floor

evidence: 109% overall net revenue retention today against the 100% floor in the objectives
56% SMB retention at which the overall falls to 100%, against 94% today
76% of ARR sits in mid-market and enterprise, where retention is 112–118%

claims.claim: Mid-market at 112% and enterprise at 118% carry it; SMB at 94% pulls it down; The targeted rise lifts it further
SMB holds 24% of ARR, so its losses move the total slowly; Even the 12% plan at twice the 2023 reaction stays far above it
Holds if mid-market and enterprise keep today's rates; A mid-market slip matters more than any SMB move; Mid-market renewal reaction is the one to watch (2a)
evidence: Annual and multi-year contracts renew on known dates

claims.claim: The retention floor is not where the risk lies; the risk is SMB customers lost to Inkwell

evidence: ARR gain at renewal $7.6M; SMB ARR repriced in 2027 $21M; SMB plan $16.8 per user; New ARR needed for 15%: None at the 2023 reaction

claims.claim: Targeted rise: Recommended / Prices where customers stay; tests SMB before betting on it

$98.9M − $93.98M − $4.3M = $0.6M left to new customers; $4.9M with no price rise

slides.title: Churn is a promotion problem
Three steps put the rise in place: reprice where customers stay, test SMB, then decide

claims.claim: Step 1 Set prices, Dec 2026–Jan 2027
evidence: 10% on mid-market renewals from January
Enterprise: 10%, or the 7% cap where it applies
Promotion cohort kept at today's price
Churn by segment and cohort on the board dashboard
Gate: leadership approval in December

claims.claim: Step 2 Test SMB, Q1 2027
evidence: 8% on a random half of non-promotion SMB renewals
The other half at $15 as the control
Churn read monthly against the control
Early mid-market renewals read the same way
Gate: extra churn under about 1 pp a month

claims.claim: Step 3 Decide and extend, Q2 2027 on
evidence: Pass: 8% on all non-promotion SMB renewals
Fail: hold SMB at $15 and study packaging
Keep reading mid-market renewal churn monthly
Midyear review against the 15% target
Exit: ARR on track for the target

claims.claim: The Q1 read decides whether SMB adds about $0.7M net or stays at $15

slides.title: 5a: A renewal test in early 2027 shows whether Inkwell has changed how SMB customers react, before we reprice them all

claims.claim: Measure the real SMB reaction to 8% at renewal against a control group
evidence: $1.3M gain before churn if 8% reaches all non-promotion SMB; about $0.7M net (3c)

claims.claim: Design: Random half of non-promotion SMB renewals at 8%, the 2023 level; Other half at $15; promotion cohort excluded
Measure: Monthly churn, test against control; Exit reasons and the win rate against Inkwell
Decide: Extend if extra churn stays under about 1 percentage point a month; Otherwise hold at $15 and study a cheaper entry plan
evidence: Gate = the 2023 spike of 0.5 percentage point × 2.1, the break-even reaction (3c). Size the test with finance so that difference is detectable

claims.claim: Owner CFO with the SMB product lead · Timing Jan–Apr 2027

slides.title: 5b: Keep the promotion cohort out of the rise, activate those who never started, and plan for the rest to leave

claims.claim: Save what onboarding can save, and stop the cohort from distorting the churn picture
evidence: $4.4M ARR in the promotion cohort at full price, the base this protects

claims.claim: Hold: No 2027 price change for the 2,100 promotion customers
Activate: Reach the 59% who never sent five documents in month one; Track activation weekly, not only churn
Plan: Count the cohort's runoff in the 2027 forecast; Report its churn apart from the rest of SMB
Learn: No more 50%-off acquisition offers without an activation test
Owner Head of Customer Success · Timing Jan–Jun 2027

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Targeted rise (Recommended): approve 10% at mid-market and enterprise renewals, 7% where capped; hold SMB at $15 and test 8% on a random half of non-promotion SMB renewals in Q1 2027, extending to all non-promotion SMB if extra churn stays under about 1 pp a month (otherwise hold at $15 and study packaging); keep the promotion cohort at today's price with an activation push; put churn by segment and cohort on the board dashboard.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Not chosen. Yields about $7.6M of ARR in 2027, not the $10.3M quoted; nets about $6.3M at the 2023 reaction, less than $4.3M beyond 2.6 times it; reprices $21M of SMB ARR before we know how SMB reacts; would put SMB plan at 1.9 times Inkwell's price. 'The 12% plan nets more only if SMB reacts mildly; the targeted rise avoids that bet.'
Recommended: $4.3M ARR gain, $0.6M left to new customers; 'Prices where customers stay; tests SMB before betting on it'.
Not chosen: 'Leaves the whole gap to new sales'; $4.9M new ARR needed.
Not in base plan; to be tested in Q1 2027. Nets about $0.7M at the 2023 reaction and breaks even at about twice that; extend if test passes.
Noted: about $0.7M more, beyond the level tested.

alternatives_considered.option: Onboarding programme to halve SMB churn (Customer Success expectation)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Onboarding is worth doing, but it is not the fix: lifting the cohort to other customers' activation cuts SMB churn by about a tenth, not half.
Left out on purpose: packaging is out of scope and the brief has no plan economics; it is the fallback if the SMB test fails.
Left out: contracts follow their own terms; changing them is outside the 2027 pricing plan.

alternatives_considered.option: New-customer sales closing the 15% gap without a price rise
alternatives_considered.treatment: Left out: the 2027 sales plan is not in the brief; the bridge shows what it must deliver.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Synthetic benchmark data: the company and all figures are fictional
Cohort churn of 4.9% is a team estimate; the brief does not report it. H1 2026 average rates applied to mid-2026 customer counts
Exit survey response rates are not given in the briefing pack
Activation estimate is generous to onboarding: assumes activating promotion customers now works as well as in their first month
Mid-market renewals are untested; the 2024 test covered new sign-ups only and the −2.1% conversion change was not statistically significant
Mid-market churn rose from 0.6% to 0.8%; cause not yet known
Mid-market deals at 200 seats or fewer are not covered by the Inkwell-absent finding
Share of enterprise ARR under 7% caps assumed the same among renewals
No price test covered enterprise; the case rests on 118% retention, 0.2% monthly churn and the advisory board finding
2023 SMB reaction is a floor for 2027, not a forecast, since no rival sold a $9 plan in 2023
SMB case: each extra lost customer counts at a full year of ARR, which overstates the loss; effects on new-customer win rates left out
How Inkwell changed existing customers' reaction is unknown
Assumes 2027 retention equals the trailing 12 months and that trailing retention holds no list-price rise (none recorded since 2023)
If retention slips a point, new customers would need to bring about $1.5M; the 2027 sales plan is not in the briefing
SMB retention of 94%: the brief does not say how much promotion churn it holds
Enterprise retention may already hold contract escalators; if so the ~$0.8M enterprise gain is partly counted twice
Net retention headroom holds if mid-market and enterprise keep today's rates

Risks: mid-market renewals react more than 2024's new sign-ups; Inkwell reaches accounts of 200 seats or fewer; SMB test misread due to too few renewals; promotion cohort keeps leaving at about 4.9% a month
Board dashboard churn figure '1.4% → 2.3%' is undefined and matches neither segment-weighted average

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text and had no images. I read chart values from the [Chart] series data and turned decimals into percentages where the axis was in %. Slides 4, 11, 16, 21 and 28 are contents/divider slides, all titled "Churn is a promotion problem". The section 1 entry is labelled only "p. 5" with no title text. Slide 34 is the appendix contents slide and has no claims. Slide 3 says "Raise prices in 2027 where customers stay for the product, and test SMB before touching it" above the numbered points, and I used that line as the governing thought. Slides 9 and 10 share the label 1d, and slides 24 and 25 share the label 4b. The next-steps table on slide 42 is listed under next_steps, not as slide claims.
